  Requirement: "Automatically reject judge changes outside verified conflict or repair paths, enforce protected-path policy, and push only after staged-diff validation." (linked issue #6231 recommendation, integrating both "conflict" and "repair" paths into the allowed set)
  Expected change site: `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` `_integration_judge_capture_baseline` and `_integration_judge_verify_scope` (around lines 8761-8891 in the post-diff layout)
  Evidence of absence: The verifier derives its allowed-path set solely from `conflicted.z` (the `git diff --diff-filter=U` snapshot of paths in merge conflict). It contains no concept of a repair-path source — no read of `_locks`, no read of `ai:implementation-failed` lineage, no scan for fix-up-issue branches, and no consultation of the orchestrator's planned-file allowlist. As written, the verifier rejects every changed path outside the conflicted set even when the change is a legitimate fix-up that was deliberately added by a follow-up implementation issue targeting the integration branch. The issue text explicitly enumerates "verified conflict or repair paths", but only "conflict paths" were implemented.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

  Requirement: "Workflow changes in this repo should usually be paired with contract tests" (`agents.md` "Repo-tree (auto-generated)" / repo convention; also enforced by the per-suite test-list pattern across `.github/workflows/ci.yml`); paired with the linked issue's explicit ask that "the committed tree must match the validated staged tree before a push" and the new behavioral assertions in `tests/test_integration_judge_scope_guard.py` covering exactly the new scope-guard logic.

  Evidence of absence: A repository-wide grep for `test_integration_judge_scope_guard` returns zero matches across `.github/workflows/`. CI uses explicit per-suite pytest invocations rather than glob discovery, so a behavioral test file that is not added to that list silently does not execute in CI. The structural-contract assertions in `tests/test_codex_agent_isolation_contract.py` were extended to lock the new call ordering and tree-validation gate, which protects the wiring, but the behavioral fixtures in `tests/test_integration_judge_scope_guard.py` (out-of-scope rejection across 4 change kinds, protected-path provenance rejection across 4 content/mode variants, ambient `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` immunity, missing-baseline fail-closed) will only run on developer machines and the release-gate `validate-scripts` job (which currently does not enumerate the new file either — it enumerates a different explicit list at `test-and-mark-stable.yml` lines 4577-4649). A future regression that swaps the projection-loop body for a too-permissive variant would not be detected by CI; only by a maintainer running the suite locally.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
